newsitem.title: USA: U.S. condemns execution of six people in Burundi.
newsitem.headline: U.S. condemns execution of six people in Burundi.

text.p: The United States on Friday condemned the execution of six people in Burundi and called on the government to halt all executions and suspend all trials related to the assassination of a Burundian president.

Burundi said the six -- three Hutus, two Tutsis and a Twa -- had played a leading role in interethnic killings in 1993, when the country's first freely elected Hutu president, Melchior Ndadaye, was murdered by Tutsi troops in an attempted coup.

But State Department spokesman James Foley said Washington was concerned that Thursday's executions would further polarise public opinion in the East African country and make ethnic peace more difficult.
He said in a statement the executions were "particularly disturbing" as Burundians prepared to meet in late August for all-party peace talks in Arusha, Tanzania.
Foley said U.S. reports indicated that five of the six people executed were members of the opposition Frodebu Party.

"The people executed may well be guilty of the crimes charged. However ... there are serious doubts by many Burundian citizens concerning the impartiality of the current judicial system -- doubts that we share," he said.

The statement called on Burundi's military rulers to halt further executions and suspend any trials arising from Ndadaye's murder and subsequent killings until negotiations had ended and an impartial system of justice was set up.
Burundi is at war, with Hutu rebels fighting the ruling Tutsi-dominated army for a greater political stake in the country.
The United States denounced the coup that brought the current military ruler, Pierre Buyoya, to power a year ago.
